intro: Built 2026-11-19 after the owner found that W40.fix-notes-editor-lines had accepted four Notes losses as 'Markdown has no form for it' (owner call 20). Three read-only surveys read every accepted bullet in ArchiveProcessor, ArchiveReader and ArchiveNotes KNOWN_ISSUES.md (122, 112 and 107 in scope) and flagged the ones whose reason hides a choice no owner call covers; the strongest were checked against the files. The W49.ki-audit-* audits had marked all of them accepted and asked about none.
excluded: Settled by an existing rule or spec, filed as work without asking: imported cluster pages left unturned (the reason, a paid call per page, is false: the free Vision rotation check exists); Claude's OpenRouter windows never sent live (a few cents, under the $7 rule); Notes search missing the linked-document names column the Notes plan specifies; Notes trimming a tab or no-break space at a title's edge (the never-lose-text rule); two contradictory Notes bullets on whether Create Extract opens a closed Extracts window (record housekeeping).
Checked and not a hidden decision: the dating route's missing propagation fallback (08-dating applies propagation only on routes with no model for the step, and every tagging run has one).
Bullets that cite an owner call, measured costs, genuine provider or platform limits, test-harness notes and fixed-defect history.

entries.title: Process Files PDFs never get the date and "sent with" lines in their header
entries.what: Live Capture writes a "Document date" line into the PDF's text header; Process Files does not, and never writes "Sent with" either, because its PDFs are made before tagging.
entries.reason: Rewriting a finished PDF was judged a risk to its tags and bytes.
entries.other: A later piece of work already rewrites these same PDFs to add the date-evidence line, so the same step could add both lines.
entries.rec_why: The rewrite the reason rules out is already done safely for another line.

entries.title: A paid batch resumed after a restart ignores the segmenter you chose
entries.what: If the app restarts while a paid overnight batch is waiting, the resumed batch splits documents as Manual does, whatever you had chosen, and a usage limit then offers only "check the rest myself".
entries.reason: The batch record does not store your choice, and using whatever Settings says now seemed riskier than Manual.
entries.other: Store the choice in the batch record, as ordinary runs already do.
entries.rec_why: The safe fallback exists only because one field was never saved; saving it removes the problem.

entries.title: The better label reader is used only if you already run a local model server
entries.what: Box and folder labels are read by the Gemma model only when LM Studio, Ollama or mlx-vlm is already running it on the Mac. Otherwise the app quietly uses the weaker Vision-plus-parser reading.
entries.reason: "By design the app starts no server and downloads no model."
entries.other: The app could offer, once, to download the model (about 8 GB) and run it while label reading is on, showing the disk and memory it needs. Most users of the suite will never have a server running.
entries.rec_why: As built, a user who has not set up a server never gets the better reading and is not told.

entries.title: One "must not train" job blocks other OpenRouter jobs running at the same time
entries.what: While any job has "must not train" on, every OpenRouter request the app makes is told to refuse training providers, so another job running at the same time without that setting can fail.
entries.reason: "Deliberately conservative."
entries.other: Attach the refusal to each job's own requests only.
entries.rec_why: You asked for the setting per collection, not for it to break unrelated jobs.

entries.title: OpenRouter models that charge per image are left out of the list
entries.what: You asked that users can run any model they prefer through OpenRouter. Models OpenRouter prices per image or per request are not listed, unmeasured Claude, Gemini and GPT models come without their makers' special handling, and the Claude-and-ChatGPT mix is not offered there.
entries.reason: The cost estimate and price cap cannot count a per-image charge; only measured models get special handling.
entries.other: List the per-image models too, marked "price not estimated". The other two limits follow from what has been measured and can stay.
entries.rec_why: Leaving a model out narrows the choice you asked for; marking its price as unknown does not.
entries.where: ArchiveProcessor/KNOWN_ISSUES.md:34, 135, 153; SUITE_TODO_DONE.md:16669 (owner: any models they prefer)

entries.title: One page Google's AI Studio will not read holds back its whole document
entries.what: For a user with no second reader set up, a page AI Studio refuses every time now holds its whole document back until a second reader is added. It used to be filed as an image without text.
entries.reason: A fix chose waiting over filing a page with no text.
entries.other: File the document with that page as image only, say so, and keep Retry for when a second reader exists.
entries.rec_why: A user with one reader is left with a stuck document and nothing to do about it.

entries.title: Finding box and folder photos in existing material relies on your colour coding
entries.what: When the app goes back over existing material, it finds box and folder label photos only by a tag or by the colour you used for them. Anyone else's photos are treated as documents.
entries.reason: Classifying every page is an OCR pass of its own, and your corpus already marks them by colour.
entries.other: Offer the label classifier as an optional pass, with its time and cost shown first.
entries.rec_why: The suite is for other users, who will not have your colour marks.

entries.title: Improve OCR refuses a file that is already searchable
entries.what: Improve OCR replaces the text page of a suite image-and-text pair. A single searchable PDF has no text page, so it is refused and you are told to reprocess it.
entries.reason: "By design, a searchable file has no text page to replace."
entries.other: Replace the hidden text layer inside the searchable file instead.
entries.rec_why: Reprocessing already does this job, and rewriting a file's hidden layer in place is the riskier path.

entries.title: Improve OCR refuses encrypted, signed and some other PDFs
entries.what: Encrypted or signed files, files in one PDF structure the bundled PDF library mishandles, single-page originals and files not in suite pairs are refused for in-place improvement.
entries.reason: Refused to keep in-place improvement safe.
entries.other: Rewrite or convert such files first, at some risk to them.
entries.rec_why: Rewriting a signed file breaks its signature, and the others would put a user's file at risk to save a reprocess.

entries.title: Intel Macs do not get the bundled compression tools
entries.what: The two compression tools shipped with the app are built for Apple-silicon Macs only. On an Intel Mac, PDFs are written uncompressed (about 2 MB a photographed page) unless the user installs the tools.
entries.reason: The tools were built on this Mac's architecture.
entries.other: Ship universal builds of both tools.
entries.rec_why: Intel Macs are few and shrinking, the run log says what to install, and the build work is not small.

entries.title: The image-and-text pair is not compressed
entries.what: The image-and-text form is 2.6 to 17 times the size of Vision OCR's output, because its image page is the full JPEG reading copy. The searchable form is compressed.
entries.reason: By design, the pair's image page is the reading copy.
entries.other: Compress the pair's image page too.
entries.rec_why: Compression is lossy, and the pair exists to keep a clean reading copy; users who want small files have the searchable form.

entries.title: No "may be read poorly" flag on routes and pages the bench never measured
entries.what: The flag that marks a page as possibly misread is not shown for readers the bench has not tested, imported pages, pages the app turned, newspaper pages read in regions or batch pages.
entries.reason: A flag's threshold is set from measured readings, and these have none.
entries.other: Apply the nearest measured threshold anyway.
entries.rec_why: A threshold fitted on other readings would raise false alarms or miss real ones; the refit adds readers as they are measured.

entries.title: Re-tagging existing PDFs does not read box or folder labels
entries.what: The route that re-tags PDFs you already have reads no labels.
entries.reason: Its outputs are its inputs, and nothing is written beside a source file.
entries.other: Write the labels into the output folder instead.
entries.rec_why: It keeps the rule that a source folder is never written to; labels can be read in an ordinary run.

entries.title: Page rotation is never asked of an OpenRouter model
entries.what: Through OpenRouter, the check for sideways pages always runs on the Mac, never through the model.
entries.reason: Written as "OpenRouter has no batch interface", which covers batch only.
entries.other: Ask the model, at a call per page.
entries.rec_why: The check on the Mac is free; only the written reason was wrong.

entries.title: The setup questions sample only photographs, not PDF pages
entries.what: When the settings interview samples your material to guess its kinds, it reads photographs only, and "No limit" on spending can be chosen only in the general settings.
entries.reason: "Design limits of the interviews."
entries.other: Render PDF pages for the sample.
entries.rec_why: It is a first-run guess that you can correct, and the extra work is small but not needed yet.

entries.title: Three small settings rules: placement by kind, unknown handwriting, renamed models
entries.what: The settings sheet sets placement by kind, not by file format; a handwritten page no classifier recognised gets no text page under "Every page"; and the rule for models that reflow text matches them by name, so a renamed build is missed.
entries.reason: Scope choices made while building settings.
entries.other: A per-format entry on the sheet; treat unknown pages as handwritten; detect reflowing by behaviour.
entries.rec_why: Each is an edge case, and a per-format choice remains in the settings file.

entries.title: Find does not scroll the text pane to the hit
entries.what: The extracted-text pane highlights the current Find hit but does not scroll to it, so you hunt for it by hand; the image pane beside it does scroll.
entries.reason: "A SwiftUI Text cannot scroll to a range."
entries.other: Build that pane with the Mac's standard text view, which can.
entries.rec_why: You asked for each hit highlighted in both panes, and the limit belongs to one component, not to macOS.

entries.title: Undoing a container edit needs the menu, and the menu just says "Undo"
entries.what: Command-Z undoes tag changes only. A container edit is undone from Edit, Undo, which does not say what it will undo.
entries.reason: SwiftUI's Edit menu does not show the action's name.
entries.other: Replace the menu's Undo item with one that names the action, and let Command-Z undo the most recent change of either kind.
entries.rec_why: Undo that cannot be found or read is close to no undo, and both fixes are standard.

entries.title: A year you retype in Finder can be overwritten by a folder's date
entries.what: If a document's text header says its year came from a stamp or an estimate and you change the year in Finder, setting a folder's date still replaces your year without asking.
entries.reason: "Finder edits are outside the suite."
entries.other: Store the year the header describes; when the document's tag no longer matches it, treat the tag as yours and leave it alone.
entries.rec_why: It replaces your own value silently, which the suite otherwise never does.

entries.title: Corrected item fields show only in the Inspector and the Zotero export
entries.what: A field you correct (an author, a title) is shown in the Inspector and exported to Zotero, but search, the list's columns and the Processor still use the old value. Corrections are made one file at a time, and renaming a file in Finder leaves them behind.
entries.reason: Nothing else showed item fields when it was built.
entries.other: Have search and the columns read the corrections. Following renames and setting several files at once can come later.
entries.rec_why: A correction you cannot search for looks like it did not take.

entries.title: Sender and recipient have no row in the Inspector
entries.what: The Inspector shows no sender or recipient for a letter.
entries.reason: No route writes them where the Reader reads, and the Reader does not read the Processor's side file.
entries.other: Read the names from the side file where the names feature puts them.
entries.rec_why: Whether the names feature writes them to that file has not been checked; a session checks, then asks again with what it found.

entries.title: After a crash mid-action, earlier undo history is gone
entries.what: If the app crashes during an action, nothing before that action can be undone afterwards, even when its writes were all recorded.
entries.reason: "The safe direction."
entries.other: Offer the earlier actions whose writes were fully recorded.
entries.rec_why: Undoing past an action that may be half done could make things worse; crashes are rare and later actions stay undoable.

entries.title: On some pages, Find marks different words in the two panes
entries.what: When a page's hidden text layer splits or misses a word, later Find hits on that page select different words in the image and text panes.
entries.reason: "Nothing in the PDF links the two panes' words better."
entries.other: Line the two texts up word by word to pair hits.
entries.rec_why: It is possible but costly for an uncommon case; the text pane's highlight is right.

entries.title: Clearing a folder's date leaves the dates it gave
entries.what: Clearing or widening a folder's date does not remove dates it already gave to documents, and choosing Not Now stops the offer until the date is edited again.
entries.reason: The offer only adds dates; Undo or the date editor takes them back.
entries.other: Offer to remove the dates it gave.
entries.rec_why: Removing dates automatically could remove ones you have since confirmed; Undo covers a mistake.

entries.title: Setting a value for many files skips dates and stops at 5,000 files
entries.what: Set for Selection works for container levels only, not dates or other marks, on up to 5,000 files.
entries.reason: Written as a save race only; the exclusions are not explained.
entries.other: Allow dates in bulk too.
entries.rec_why: Folder dates already reach every document in a folder; a bulk date for an arbitrary selection is rarely right.

entries.title: Two Containers limits: nested folder maps and the 100-value menu
entries.what: The folder-levels sheet edits only the top folder's map, not one set in a subfolder, and the Containers menu lists each facet's 100 most common values across the whole library.
entries.reason: A bound on the menu's length; the sheet sets the tree's own levels.
entries.other: Edit nested maps; narrow the menu by the other facets chosen.
entries.rec_why: Both are edge cases; a nested map can still be edited by hand.

entries.title: VoiceOver and keyboard users cannot use the source chips in a note
entries.what: The buttons on a source or passage chip (Jump, Reveal, Preview, Open in Zotero) cannot be reached by VoiceOver or the keyboard.
entries.reason: Written as a test-tool limit: "may not be possible", "not attempted".
entries.other: Give each chip an accessibility element and keyboard commands for the chip under the cursor, or put its actions in a right-click menu.
entries.rec_why: It is a real accessibility gap that was never tried, and a menu or keyboard route is ordinary work.

entries.title: Notes can write into an archive folder it was never given, without asking
entries.what: Choosing a store folder or archive folder inside an archive that Notes has not been given starts a new store, or writes a new identity file, there. Links copied from the real archive then do not match it.
entries.reason: "The sandbox gives Notes the picked folder only, not its parents."
entries.other: Before writing, ask whether the folder is the top of an archive, and offer to choose the archive folder first.
entries.rec_why: The sandbox limit is real, but what to do about it was a choice; one question stops a silent second identity.

entries.title: A jump into a note you are editing can land at the top instead of the passage
entries.what: If you jump to a passage in the note you are editing in the same window, the note can open at the top instead of at the passage.
entries.reason: "The realistic jump is cross-window."
entries.other: Save the edit and refresh the note before scrolling.
entries.rec_why: The fix is small, and landing at the wrong place loses your position.

entries.title: Two windows pasting a same-named image in the same second
entries.what: With one note open in two windows, pasting images with the same name in both within the same second leaves the second as a "Missing" placeholder.
entries.reason: A shared name authority cannot serve two windows.
entries.other: One name list per note, shared by its windows.
entries.rec_why: It needs two windows on one note and a same-second paste; the cost outweighs the case.

entries.title: An image outside a note's assets folder shows as "Blocked"
entries.what: An image written into a note by hand that sits outside the note's assets folder shows "Blocked" instead of loading.
entries.reason: Deliberate: the assets folder is the boundary, and moving the file in recovers it.
entries.other: Allow images anywhere in the note's own folder, or offer to move them in.
entries.rec_why: It keeps notes from reading files they do not own; revisit if the DEVONthink import resumes.
